title: Eleven years of orthokeratology contact lens wear for slowing myopia progression in children

groups.description: overnight orthokeratology (Menicon Z Night, tisilfocon A), chosen at baseline; nonrandomized MCOS trial, Madrid, Spain; White European children (mean age of the 31 recruited, T1)
distance single-vision spectacles, chosen at baseline; controls who changed to single-vision soft contact lenses after the first 2 years stayed in this group (mean age of the 30 recruited, T1)

notes: Part of a nonrandomized clinical trial (MCOS; ClinicalTrials.gov NTC04806763 and NTC04806711): White European children 6–12 years, myopia −0.75 to −4.00 DS, astigmatism ≤ 1.00 DC, free choice at baseline of orthokeratology or distance single-vision spectacles (a pre-treatment allocation); Novovision clinic, Madrid, Spain.
AL by IOLMaster 500 (Zeiss), mean of three measurements; right eye only; units mm (T1 and T2).

Visits every 6 months for the first 2 years; subjects were contacted about 5 and 9 years after the 2-year study (about 7 and 11 years from baseline). Recruited 31 orthokeratology and 30 control; 29 and 24 completed 2 years; 14 and 16 attended at 7 years; 10 and 15 at 11 years.

Subjects who switched lens modality were excluded from the analyses; control subjects who changed from single-vision spectacles to single-vision soft contact lenses after 2 years were retained; interruptions of orthokeratology wear after 2 years were not systematically recorded (Discussion).
Refraction (MSE), keratometry, corneal shape and pupil diameter are tabulated (T1) and not used.
